question: What kinds of drugs can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:No drugs affect driving if taken as directed.,c:Only prescription medicines.,d:Over-the-counter
note: Many drugs — illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter — may impair driving and make it unsafe or illegal to drive.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks open, what is the correct response?
options: a:Shift to neutral, turn on hazard lights, apply brakes gradually, and safely pull off the road, then turn off the ignition.,b:Slam the brakes and hold them down hard.,c:Keep accelerating to reach a safe area quickly.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply to stall the engine.
note: If the throttle sticks, shift to neutral and safely slow to the side while using brakes and hazards; then turn off the engine when safe.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, the safest way to pass a bicyclist is to:
options: a:Honk and expect the bicyclist to move over.,b:Force them off the road by driving quickly past.,c:Pass as close as possible to minimize time near them.,d:Slow down
note: Give bicyclists at least 3 feet of space (more at higher speeds or with groups) and only pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs legally indicate?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area.,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed under ideal conditions.,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.,d:A recommended speed for inexperienced drivers.
note: Speed limit signs state the maximum or minimum legal speeds under ideal conditions; drivers must reduce speed when conditions require it.

question: Why is a leaking exhaust system hazardous?
options: a:Carbon monoxide poisoning.,b:A loss of hearing.,c:Pollution.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment, which can be deadly; repair exhaust leaks promptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,b:Use mirrors and blind-spot checks and use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed.,c:Enter immediately without checking.,d:Yield only to vehicles on your left.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to traffic already on the freeway.

question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Safely pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,c:Ignore it if you do not see lights.,d:Stop immediately where you are and remain.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches from behind, create a clear path by pulling to the right and stopping when safe to do so.

question: Which factor greatly increases stopping distance and the seriousness of a crash?
options: a:Night driving.,b:Slow speeds,c:High speeds
note: Higher speeds greatly increase stopping distance and the potential severity of a crash; driving faster increases impact force.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: a:Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,b:You must not cross for any reason.,c:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it is safe.,d:It marks a bicycle lane.
note: A single broken yellow line separates opposing traffic and permits passing from either side when it’s safe.

question: At a railroad crossing without flashing warnings or gates, how should you proceed?
options: a:Approach with caution and be prepared to yield to any train, ensuring room to clear the tracks.,b:Cross immediately to save time.,c:Always stop no matter what.,d:Shift gears while crossing to avoid stalling.
note: When no signals or gates exist, approach carefully, look both ways, and only cross when you are sure no train is coming and there is space to clear the tracks.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Pull to the right curb and stop.,c:Keep driving in your lane and ignore it.,d:Speed up to clear the way.
note: Immediately pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

question: If you are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Check mirrors only and change lanes.,b:Check mirrors and look over your left shoulder before changing.,c:Check mirrors,d:Signal and immediately swing into the right lane.
note: When moving right, check mirrors, signal, and look over the right shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: Where should you try to maintain a space cushion when driving?
options: a:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,b:On all sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of your vehicle.
note: Maintain a cushion of space around your vehicle—front, rear, and sides—so you have time to react to hazards.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited in both directions.,b:Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:You may pass if no oncoming traffic appears.,d:You may use the shoulder to pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate lanes of opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a solid red light (where allowed), you must:
options: a:Only signal after you begin turning.,b:Come to a complete stop,c:Turn immediately without stopping.,d:Wait for the light to turn green no matter what.
note: Unless prohibited by sign, you may turn right on red after a full stop and after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from a driveway or private road, you should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles on your left only.,b:Drive quickly onto the road to merge.,c:Yield to traffic on the highway.,d:Assume you have the right-of-way.
note: Yield to all vehicles already on the roadway and merge only when it is safe.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:Only if there are no other vehicles on the road.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:Only during daylight.,d:Never.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes or pass.

question: When driving in fog you should use:
options: a:High beam headlights to see further.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Hazard lights while moving.,d:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).
note: Use low beams and fog lights where available; high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the approaching vehicle's wheels.,c:Toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.,d:Directly into the headlights to show them you're blinded.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams while keeping enough view to stay on course.

question: When changing lanes on most roads, you should:
options: a:Make a lane change without checking blind spots to be quick.,b:Begin signaling well before the lane change and check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Signal as you start the lane change and then check your mirrors.,d:Only check mirrors and then change lanes without signaling.
note: Signal early (about 100 feet in residential areas or 5 seconds on a freeway), check mirrors and blind spots before moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Turn around because the intersection is closed.,c:Proceed through the intersection with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; be prepared to yield as needed.

question: When are roads most dangerous in terms of traction relative to rain?
options: a:After it has been raining for several hours.,b:Just as it begins to rain,c:When it stops raining completely.,d:Only during heavy thunderstorms.
note: Light initial rain mixes with surface oil and dirt, creating a slick film that makes roads especially hazardous at the start of a rain.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to go through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing to verify no cross traffic.,b:After stopping at least 20 feet from the intersection.,c:After coming to a complete stop and confirming it's safe.,d:After yielding to pedestrians only.
note: If there's no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed further.,b:Not allow other cars to pass your vehicle.,c:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and continue slowly.
note: If you impede the normal flow of traffic by driving too slowly on a two-lane road, you are required to pull off and let others pass safely.

question: If you suffer a tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator, do not immediately brake hard, gradually slow, and pull off the road.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately to stop quickly.,c:Turn the steering wheel sharply to the right and stop in the travel lane.,d:Speed up to reduce wobble.
note: If a tire blows, ease off the gas, avoid sudden braking, steer straight while slowing, and pull safely off the roadway.

question: When it starts to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Maintain normal following distance but increase speed to get home faster.,b:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase your following distance.,c:Turn on your high beams to better see the road ahead.,d:Ignore other vehicles and drive normally.
note: In snowy or icy conditions keep windows clear and allow extra stopping distance because roads will be slippery.

question: If stopped by a police officer, how should you behave?
options: a:Get out immediately and approach the officer.,b:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,c:Open your door and shout your license number.,d:Unbuckle your seat belt and exit the vehicle.
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands visible and wait for the officer to approach; only retrieve documents when requested.

question: Which of these can impair driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication.,c:A lack of sleep.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs (including some medications), and by drowsiness or lack of sleep.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and can't find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Must stay until police arrive.,b:Leave,c:Drive to the nearest service station.,d:Leave a written notice with your name
note: If you cannot locate the owner, leave a written notice with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident.

question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.,b:Honk to alert them before passing.,c:Slow down and give as much space as possible.,d:Pass quickly without changing lane position.
note: Slow down and allow as much lateral space as possible when passing bicyclists; do not crowd them.

question: Does drinking coffee after alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Yes — it cancels the alcohol's effect.,b:No — it does not affect BAC.,c:It instantly sober you up.,d:It increases BAC.
note: Caffeine or coffee does not lower BAC; it may make you more alert but does not reduce alcohol levels in your system.

question: Where are stop lines painted and what do they indicate?
options: a:In curves and on hills.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines across lanes at intersections and crosswalks showing where drivers must stop their vehicle.

question: What is the recommended response when another driver behaves aggressively?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact
note: If confronted by an aggressive driver, stay calm, avoid eye contact, slow down, and allow them to pass. Do not engage or retaliate.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do if you are not involved?
options: a:Keep your attention on your driving and pass without stopping unless emergency help hasn't arrived and you can safely assist.,b:Stop and get out to watch the scene.,c:Pile into the area to take photographs.,d:Slow down to look and impede traffic.
note: Do not stop at accident scenes unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely assist—keep moving and stay alert.

question: How can you best avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Say no when someone offers you a drink if you're already drinking.,c:Drink water between alcoholic drinks so you can drive later.
note: The only reliable way to avoid alcohol-impaired driving is to plan ahead and decide not to drive before drinking begins, because alcohol impairs judgment.

question: How should you approach a railroad crossing that has no signals?
options: a:Speed through to minimize time on the tracks.,b:Slow down,c:Always stop regardless of visibility.,d:Assume crossings without signals are always safe.
note: At unsignaled crossings, slow and be ready to stop; look and listen for approaching trains before proceeding.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while using prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:Nothing significant will occur.,b:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,c:The alcohol will make the medicine more effective.,d:The medicine will cancel the alcohol's effects.
note: Mixing alcohol with medications can amplify impairing effects and produce greater impairment than either substance alone.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:To signal impatience in traffic.,b:When passing another car.,c:If you've lost control of your vehicle to warn others.,d:To greet friends driving nearby.
note: Use your horn to warn others of danger — for example, if you have lost control — not to express frustration.

question: What does a crossbuck sign identify?
options: a:School zones.,b:Railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings and indicate drivers must yield to trains. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it allowed to cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving passenger car when safe.,b:To pass another car going the same direction.,c:To make a left turn into or from a driveway,d:To overtake bicyclists at any time.
note: Double solid lines prohibit passing or lane changes; crossing is permitted only for left turns into/from driveways or similar maneuvers where allowed.

question: Which of these is a common cause of traffic collisions?
options: a:Excessive speed for conditions,b:Following other vehicles too closely.,c:Inattentive driving
note: While inattentiveness and tailgating contribute to crashes, driving at excessive speeds for the conditions is a major cause of serious collisions.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer vs. wine) change how alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:No — impairment depends on amount consumed,b:Only hard liquor impairs driving.,c:Yes — mixed drinks are more impairing.,d:Yes — beer affects you less than wine.
note: All types of alcoholic beverages impair reflexes and judgment based on the amount consumed, not the type.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, how should you react?
options: a:Call the police immediately while driving erratically.,b:Try to block them from passing.,c:Flash your lights to reprimand them.,d:Stay calm and move out of their way.
note: Remain calm and get out of the aggressive driver's way to avoid escalation or a crash.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather.,b:Poor road design.,c:Human error.,d:Mechanical failure.
note: Most crashes result from human error such as inattention, misjudgment, or unsafe actions.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching with siren or lights, what should you do?
options: a:Drive as far right as possible and stop, taking care not to stop in an intersection.,b:Continue at the same speed if you are not in the emergency vehicle's path.,c:Speed up and pull away from the emergency vehicle.,d:Stop immediately in your lane wherever you are.
note: On two-lane roads you must pull as far right as safe and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is important.,b:Snow tires can improve traction.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,d:Winter is the most difficult driving season.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow, ice, rain, or similar hazardous conditions—winter requires extra caution and preparation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Traffic signals sometimes display arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid yellow arrow mean?
options: a:It indicates a pedestrian-only phase is starting.,b:It is never used in traffic signals.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light and you should prepare to stop.,d:It means you may immediately turn in the arrow's direction without yielding.
note: A solid yellow arrow functions like a steady yellow light for that turn; you should slow and prepare to stop as a red arrow is imminent.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these statements about passing is true?
options: a:You should return to your lane before seeing the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes,c:Do not signal when passing to avoid confusion.,d:Only use your mirrors
note: When passing, signal early, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear; return when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Go through the intersection quickly.,b:The signal is malfunctioning.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop,d:Yield to other cars and continue at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal will soon be red; slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.

question: What type of signs warn drivers about hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Guide signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Warning signs.,d:Regulatory signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions and require caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:
options: a:Only yield to traffic on your left.,b:Always come to a complete stop,c:Ignore it if no traffic is present.,d:Slow and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the roadway you are entering.
note: A yield sign requires slowing and giving right-of-way to traffic on the roadway you plan to enter or cross.

question: Why must drivers be extra alert to motorcycles, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They always travel at the same speed as cars.,b:They are smaller and harder to see,c:They obey completely different laws.,d:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Smaller road users can be difficult to detect; drivers should actively scan for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians to avoid collisions.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, your first step should be to:
options: a:Reverse quickly into the space.,b:Pull up even with the car in front of the space before beginning to back in.,c:Turn your wheels immediately toward the curb.,d:Angle into the space without aligning with neighboring cars.
note: Stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space before beginning maneuvers to back into the parking spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign.,b:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,c:At a red traffic light.,d:All of the above.
note: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicates:
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe, while those next to the solid line may not.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Both lanes may pass at any time.,d:The road is one-way.
note: When the broken line is beside your lane, you may pass when safe; drivers next to the solid line may not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it unsafe and illegal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On the shoulder of the road when safe.,b:When the passing lane is clear and marked with a broken yellow line.,c:On a hill or in a curve where you cannot see oncoming traffic.,d:On a multilane expressway with three lanes.
note: Passing in curves or on hills is unsafe because you can’t see oncoming traffic; passing on the shoulder is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the usual speed limit on open county highways in West Virginia?
options: a:65 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:70 mph.,d:60 mph.
note: In West Virginia, open county highways ordinarily have a 55 mph speed limit unless signs indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a:Signal only when other vehicles are present.,b:Signal briefly as you begin the turn only.,c:Always signal your intentions in advance,d:Signal only at night.
note: Always use your signal before turning or changing lanes to inform other road users of your intentions.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:The same if headlights are used.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.,d:Less dangerous.
note: Night driving is more dangerous due to reduced visibility, glare, and more fatigued or impaired drivers.

question: If an approaching vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you look to avoid glare?
options: a:The right side of the road.,b:The center of the road.,c:Either side at random.,d:Directly into the headlights.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while still maintaining position on your lane until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Stop on the ramp and wait for an opening in traffic.,b:Enter at any speed,c:Adjust your speed to match traffic and merge safely after locating a gap.,d:Drive on the shoulder briefly and merge when safe.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed, locate a gap, and merge without stopping on the ramp.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When you need to warn another road user of immediate danger, such as a child stepping into the street.,b:When traveling through an intersection.,c:To greet acquaintances on the sidewalk.,d:When passing a bicyclist on a quiet road.
note: Use your horn as a warning to prevent collisions — for example, to alert someone who may step into traffic unexpectedly.

question: What must a driver do when an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop immediately.,b:Slow down and continue driving to the right.,c:Turn on four-way flashers and continue moving.,d:Speed up to clear the lane.
note: When approached by an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, you must drive to the right and stop until it has passed.

question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When crossing would interfere with traffic or be unsafe.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When the vehicle in front is disabled.,d:When passing is allowed.
note: You may cross broken lines to pass or change lanes only if it is safe and does not interfere with traffic.

question: A pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn continuously.,b:Speed up and pass in front of them.,c:Flash your lights to warn them.,d:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Always yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway and be prepared to stop, especially in crosswalks and near children.

question: What must you do when you see a steady green arrow at a traffic signal?
options: a:Always stop and wait for a green circular light.,b:Merge immediately without yielding.,c:Turn only if there is no oncoming traffic at any speed.,d:You may turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A green arrow permits the indicated turn, but you must still yield to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Turn on hazards.,b:Slow and stop if safe unless already in the intersection.,c:Ignore it because green still has priority.,d:Speed up to beat the red.
note: A steady yellow warns that red is coming; stop if you can do so safely unless you're already in the intersection.

question: Before starting the vehicle, what safety step should you do?
options: a:Buckle your seat belt and ensure passengers are buckled.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.,d:Start the car and then buckle.
note: Develop a routine of buckling your seat belt and ensuring all passengers are restrained before switching on the ignition.

question: What best describes defensive driving?
options: a:Racing to get ahead of poor drivers.,b:Following the vehicle ahead closely to control traffic.,c:Identifying hazardous driving situations and acting to avoid crashes.
note: Defensive driving means recognizing potential hazards early and taking actions to prevent conflicts and crashes.

question: How should a seat belt be properly worn?
options: a:Is loose.,b:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Is hidden beneath the seat.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across the hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should lie across the chest and shoulder, not the neck or face.

question: Which of the following does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:You are less alert.,b:You become more alert.,c:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,d:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, impairs judgment of speed and distance, and reduces alertness—becoming more alert does not happen after drinking.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Red.,b:White.,c:Blue.,d:Yellow.
note: Yellow center lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving the same direction.

question: When driving in poor weather, drivers should:
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Increase their following distance.,c:Maintain the same following distance as in good weather.,d:Increase their speed to clear hazardous areas quicker.
note: Increase following distance in bad weather since stopping distances are longer and unexpected hazards are more likely.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Steer in the direction of the skid (turn the wheel into the skid) and avoid overcorrecting.,b:Turn the steering wheel into oncoming traffic always.,c:Brake hard and hold the wheel firmly straight.,d:Turn away from the skid and slam the brakes.
note: When skidding, remain calm and steer in the skid direction until you regain traction; avoid overcorrection.

question: How must a driver behave toward pedestrians in or near the roadway?
options: a:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians,c:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of your vehicle before proceeding.
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid hitting pedestrians; you should yield to pedestrians even if they are crossing improperly.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:That children will always wait for traffic to clear.,b:That a child may suddenly run into the street without looking.,c:That children will remain on the sidewalk.,d:That children will obey crossing guards at all times.
note: Children may not recognize hazards and can dart into the street unexpectedly; slow down and be prepared to stop.

question: When driving on highways, how should you maintain alertness?
options: a:Stare straight ahead to avoid distractions.,b:Rely on cruise control exclusively.,c:Keep your eyes moving and be ready to react to hazards.,d:Look at one thing for a long time to focus.
note: Avoid highway hypnosis by scanning the road, checking mirrors, and being prepared for sudden hazards.

question: Which traffic control device requires you to come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield, then proceed when the way is clear.

question: Before backing out of a driveway with children nearby, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn loudly to warn children.,b:Exit the vehicle and walk to the rear to ensure the way is clear.,c:Rev the engine so they notice you are moving.,d:Back up slowly while watching through mirrors only.
note: Because children are hard to see from the driver's seat, get out and check behind your vehicle before backing into or out of a driveway.

question: If a transit (bus) is signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping, you must:
options: a:Remain in your lane and ignore the signal.,b:Speed past before they merge.,c:Yield and allow them to safely re-enter.,d:Sound your horn to warn them.
note: Yield — by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping if necessary — to let buses re-enter traffic after loading/unloading.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly; always exercise caution to avoid hitting pedestrians.

question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:If possible,d:Stop immediately in your lane.
note: Give stopped emergency or roadside vehicles as much space as possible by changing lanes or slowing down safely if a lane change is unsafe.

question: What colors are used on highway signs that tell you distances or destinations (such as the next exit)?
options: a:Red background with white letters.,b:Black background with white letters.,c:Yellow background with black letters.,d:Green background with white letters.
note: Destination and distance signs on highways are green with white letters or symbols.

question: Your blind spot refers to the area:
options: a:Directly behind your vehicle as seen in the rearview mirror.,b:You cannot see without moving your head (not visible in mirrors).,c:Inside the vehicle cabin near the driver.,d:Covered by your side mirrors.
note: Blind spots are those areas to the sides and rear you cannot see in your mirrors without turning your head.

question: When must you stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children?
options: a:If it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.,b:When it approaches you even if its lights are not flashing.,c:If you are driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing or its stop arm extended. Remain stopped as long as the red lights are flashing and/or the stop arm is out.

question: On which signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A solid green circular light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A green arrow pointing left.,d:A steady red arrow to the left.
note: A steady green arrow pointing left gives protected left-turn movement and the right-of-way; oncoming traffic is stopped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on an uphill, what should you expect?
options: a:It is always legal to pass on a hill if you have room.,b:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted limit and you may not be able to safely pass on a hill.,c:The truck will always keep up with posted speeds.,d:The truck will automatically pull over to let you pass.
note: Large vehicles often slow on inclines; passing on hills with limited sight distance is unsafe and may be illegal.

question: Which statement is correct about alcohol's effect on driving?
options: a:Alcohol does not affect driving when consumed with food.,b:Even small amounts of alcohol can impair concentration,c:Only a BAC above the legal limit impairs driving.,d:Alcohol improves calmness and reaction time.
note: Any alcohol intake impairs cognitive functions and driving skills; no amount is completely safe for driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using emergency signals, you should:
options: a:Continue driving in a normal manner, you are not required to yield unless it is using sirens or lights.,b:Pull over and stop immediately.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.,d:Stop in the middle of the street to allow it by.
note: You only need to yield and clear a path when an emergency vehicle is using its lights and/or siren; otherwise continue normally.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should turn the steering wheel:
options: a:To keep the front wheels straight and locked.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid immediately.,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go (into the skid).,d:Sharp and fast away from the skid.
note: When skidding, steer into the direction you want the car to go; as it straightens, correct the steering to avoid overcorrection.

question: How can you help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Reduce speed in the rain.,b:Keep tires properly inflated.,c:All of the above.,d:Ensure tires have good tread depth.
note: Prevent hydroplaning by reducing speed in wet conditions and maintaining proper tire pressure and tread depth.

question: Where do pedestrians have the right-of-way?
options: a:At an intersection crosswalk.,b:When crossing an alley or driveway.,c:If they are blind and using a cane or guide dog.,d:All of the above.
note: Pedestrians in crosswalks, crossing driveways/alleys, and blind pedestrians using aids have the right-of-way.

question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Turn from any lane as long as the turn signal is on.,b:Speed up and cut in front of oncoming traffic.,c:Stop in the intersection before turning.,d:Signal in advance
note: Signal early, position in the left lane as appropriate, check for oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and slow smoothly before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Speeding can kill.,b:Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.,c:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Both driving excessively fast and driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous; driving significantly below the flow of traffic on highways may cause unsafe passing maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what is the correct action?
options: a:Start the turn into only the first lane and complete it later.,b:Accelerate quickly when the first lane is clear.,c:Expect oncoming drivers to wave you through.,d:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before making the turn.
note: Do not begin the left turn until you have clear sight of all lanes you need to cross and can complete the maneuver safely.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.,b:Pull to the curb,c:Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
note: If you hear an emergency vehicle and cannot locate it, safely pull to the right and stop until you are sure it is not approaching your position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit.,d:Cross several lanes at the last second to reach it.
note: If you miss an exit, proceed to the next one—do not stop, back up, turn across the median, or make other illegal maneuvers on the highway.

question: When is it permissible to park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If you turn on your emergency flashers.,b:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,c:To consult a map.,d:Only in an emergency.
note: Parking on the shoulder of a freeway is prohibited except in emergencies.

question: How often does West Virginia require a state inspection of vehicles?
options: a:Only upon initial registration.,b:Every year.,c:Only if the vehicle is over 10 years old.,d:Every two years.
note: West Virginia requires an annual safety inspection to ensure vehicles are in safe driving condition.

question: When meeting a vehicle with blinding headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to pass quickly.,b:Flash your lights repeatedly.,c:Use your high beams until they dim theirs.,d:Look to the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.
note: Avoid looking directly at blinding headlights; focus on the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.

question: What is a potential penalty for a first DUI offense in West Virginia?
options: a:Three years in the state penitentiary and a $3,b:No penalties for first offense.,c:Possible jail time (up to six months depending on circumstances),d:Two months in county jail and a $30 fine.
note: A first DUI conviction can include fines, possible jail time (up to six months depending on factors), and license suspension; penalties increase with aggravating factors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is the driver signaling?
options: a:Turning left.,b:Turning right.,c:Speeding up.,d:Stopping.
note: A left arm extended upward is the hand signal for a right turn.

question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle using lights or siren?
options: a:Only when other vehicles yield first.,b:Never,c:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens by pulling to the right and stopping.

question: How is distracted driving characterized?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Not a safety concern.,c:Extremely risky behavior.,d:Only a problem for new drivers.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky and significantly increases the chance of a crash.

question: Are you ever allowed to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:If traffic is heavy and you are late for an appointment.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the train has passed and gates are still down.,d:When the lights stop flashing.
note: You must not go around lowered crossing gates—stop and wait until gates are fully raised and signals indicate it is safe to proceed.

question: Which of the following about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You never need to stop at a crossing with a stop sign.,b:You may always drive around gates if no train is visible.,c:Crossings with gates are optional and may be ignored.,d:It is illegal to go around lowered gates
note: Do not go around lowered gates, obey flags and lights when present, and remember some crossings lack active warning devices.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the left.,b:Either vehicle may proceed with no yielding.,c:Yield only if one vehicle signals.,d:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: At intersections where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The pedestrian.,b:Whoever is slower.,c:Whoever started moving last.,d:The driver.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the road even when there's no traffic signal.

question: Compared with smaller cars, larger vehicles typically have:
options: a:No blind spots due to mirrors.,b:Smaller blind spots than compact cars.,c:Automatic sensors that eliminate blind spots.,d:Much larger blind spots.
note: Large trucks and buses have extensive blind areas; avoid lingering alongside where the driver cannot see you.

question: What does an \End school zone sign indicate?"
options: a:That a crosswalk is ahead.,b:That the speed limit is 20 mph.,c:The start of a reduced-speed school zone.,d:The end of the reduced school-zone speed limit.
note: An End School Zone sign indicates the reduced school-zone speed restriction has ended.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Turn on high-beam headlights.,b:Turn on windshield wipers.,c:Stop immediately in the travel lane.,d:Reduce your speed.
note: Reducing speed is the first action to compensate for decreased visibility and increased risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you come to an intersection displaying a flashing red light?
options: a:Wait for a flashing green light.,b:Ignore it and continue driving normally.,c:Come to a full stop,d:Slow and pass through if clear.
note: Treat a flashing red light as a stop sign: stop completely and proceed only when safe.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance becomes longer when you are stopping:
options: a:On dry paved highways.,b:When driving at night under clear conditions.,c:When your vehicle is unloaded and light.,d:On wet or icy pavement.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet, icy, or loose surfaces and when tires or brakes are not optimal.

question: What should you do when driving in foggy conditions?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Drive at the maximum speed limit.,c:Turn on your low beam headlights.,d:Turn on your hazard lights.
note: Use low-beam headlights and reduce speed when visibility is reduced; high beams reflect back and worsen visibility.

question: What does an orange-colored traffic sign typically indicate?
options: a:The start of a no-passing zone.,b:Construction or maintenance ahead.,c:A hospital nearby.,d:A school zone ahead.
note: Orange signs warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations and advise extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:When a passing zone ends.,b:Only after signaling for five seconds.,c:When there's enough room between you and the passed vehicle.,d:Immediately after passing regardless of distance.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it's safe to do so.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which of the following?
options: a:The effect that amphetamines have.,b:The effect that anger has.,c:The effect that alcohol has.,d:The effect that caffeine has.
note: Fatigue impairs driving in ways similar to alcohol intoxication; for example, 18 hours awake can impair you about as much as a 0.05% BAC and 24 hours about 0.10% BAC.

question: When driving in rain, you must use which headlights?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:No lights are necessary in daylight rain.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rainy conditions so other drivers can see your vehicle and to reduce glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver who is traveling much slower than the normal flow of traffic do?
options: a:Refuse to allow cars to pass behind them.,b:Accelerate to the speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:Pull off the road at the earliest safe point to let traffic pass if it is causing a backup.,d:Always stay in the left lane.
note: If driving significantly below normal traffic speed and causing backups on a two-lane road, the driver must pull off when safe to allow others to pass.

question: A telltale sign of a drunk driver often includes:
options: a:Driving steadily at the speed limit.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Carefully signaling every move.,d:Always obeying traffic laws.
note: Common indicators of impaired driving include weaving, sudden lane changes, erratic speeds, and abrupt stops.

question: What is the most important speed-management rule for navigating curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve so inertia doesn't push you outward.,b:Speed up before the curve and brake in the sharpest part.,c:Maintain posted speed and brake hard mid-curve.,d:Use engine braking only while in the curve.
note: Reduce speed prior to entering a curve to maintain control; avoid braking hard while turning if possible.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train, you must stop if:
options: a:Never,b:A stop sign is posted or crossing lights are flashing or gates are lowered.,c:Only if a train is visible.,d:Only if a flagger is present.
note: Stop when flashing red lights are active, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, or other official signals require stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:
options: a:The traffic signal is broken so you may proceed as usual.,b:You do not have to stop if no other cars are present.,c:You must slow but not stop.,d:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop
note: A flashing red requires a full stop, just like a stop sign, before proceeding when clear.

question: In cold or wet weather, which road sections freeze more quickly and stay icy longer?
options: a:Flat open areas exposed to the sun.,b:Shaded areas (sections of road shaded by trees or buildings).,c:Curvy sections of road.,d:Roads with many streetlights.
note: Shaded parts of the roadway freeze before and thaw after surrounding areas; they are the last to dry and the most likely to be icy in cold or wet conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make a quick U-turn.,b:Continue to the next exit or safe turnaround.,c:Cut across lanes to return to the exit.,d:Stop and back up on the shoulder.
note: Do not back up on a freeway; proceed to the next exit or a safe place to turn around.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution — slow down and be alert for hazards.

question: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, you must stop from both directions at what approximate distance?
options: a:You must stop before reaching the bus, do not proceed until lights stop (no specific feet required in this question).,b:Within 50 feet of the bus.,c:Within 30 feet of the bus.,d:Within 10 feet of the bus.
note: Traffic from both directions must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights until the bus resumes motion and lights are off.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Turn off the ignition immediately while moving.,b:Brake hard and shift into neutral immediately.,c:Work harder to steer,d:Honk and continue at the same speed to the nearest exit.
note: If power steering stops, more effort is needed to steer—slow down, steadily steer to a safe location, and stop.

question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply to the left so you can complete the turn quickly.,b:Flash your headlights to alert other drivers.,c:Turn your wheels to the right as a precaution.,d:Keep your wheels straight while signaling and waiting.
note: Keep the wheels straight while waiting to turn so a rear-end collision will not push you into oncoming traffic.

question: Signs indicating areas of public recreation typically have which color?
options: a:Green.,b:Orange.,c:Red.,d:Brown.
note: Brown signs denote cultural or recreational areas, such as parks and historic sites.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,d:The vehicle that honks first has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: If you are taking a non-prescription drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the labels for warnings about driving and side effects.,b:Drink alcohol instead to counteract side effects.,c:Ignore label warnings if you feel fine.,d:Double the dose to build tolerance.
note: Many over-the-counter medications can impair driving; read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure whether a drug affects your driving ability.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes moving in the same direction where passing is not allowed.,b:Lanes moving in the same direction that may be crossed to pass when safe.,c:Lanes moving in opposite directions where passing is prohibited.,d:A no-passing zone.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed for passing when safe.

question: What is the first adjustment you should make when getting into a car to drive?
options: a:Adjust your seat to a comfortable and safe driving position.,b:Buckle your seat belt after moving the seat.,c:Adjust the steering wheel before the seat.,d:Adjust the radio to a low volume.
note: Set your seat first so you can reach controls and see clearly, then adjust mirrors, steering wheel, and seat belt as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive at a speed greater than:
options: a:The posted maximum speed limit.,b:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,c:A speed the driver prefers.,d:A speed that shortcuts traffic.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions — even if below the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you behave when a funeral procession approaches an intersection you are waiting at?
options: a:Expect the procession to yield to you.,b:Yield to the procession after the lead vehicle crosses the intersection.,c:Try to beat the lead vehicle through the intersection.
note: While not legally required in all cases, courtesy is to yield to a funeral procession; once the lead vehicle clears the intersection, allow the procession to pass.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what checks should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head without using mirrors.,b:Only check your rearview mirror.,c:Sound your horn before moving.,d:Check your side and rearview mirrors
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and then look over your shoulder immediately before moving to ensure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods and failing to actively scan.,b:Frequent rest stops during a long trip.,c:Getting too much sleep the night before driving.
note: Highway hypnosis occurs when a driver stares ahead for long stretches and stops actively scanning, which can lead to zoning out and delayed reactions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another motorist is trying to pass your vehicle, what is the correct action?
options: a:Signal when you want the other driver to pass.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
note: When another driver is passing, stay in your lane, check for oncoming traffic, and adjust speed if necessary to let them return to their lane safely.

question: What does a solid yellow line beside your lane signify?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Do not pass.,c:Pass with caution.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane indicates passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: Which is important for safe night driving?
options: a:Never drive if you are tired.,b:Ensure your headlights work.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night, increase following distance to allow more reaction time, be well-rested, and verify all lights are functioning.

question: Why must drivers take care when passing bicyclists?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:You are moving faster than the bicycle.
note: Cyclists may swerve to avoid obstacles and oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass, so give bicycles plenty of space.

question: Why must drivers be more careful at night?
options: a:Traffic moves faster at night.,b:There is more traffic at night.,c:Drivers cannot see as well at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards, pedestrians, and other vehicles. Use headlights and increase caution.

question: Why should you avoid following too closely behind another vehicle?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You might not have time to stop if the car ahead brakes suddenly.,c:You may miss the vehicle's turn signals.,d:It helps you travel faster.
note: Following too closely reduces your reaction time and braking distance, increasing the risk of collision if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

question: Which recommendation does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Having heavily tinted windows that reduce visibility at night is safe.,b:Keep the windshield clean to reduce glare.,c:Carry a flashlight in the vehicle for emergencies.,d:Be aware that tinted windows can reduce darkness visibility.
note: Tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility and are not advisable for safe night driving; keep windshield clean and carry a flashlight.

question: Which practice can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Refuse to use turn signals so others adapt.,b:Tailgate slower drivers to keep traffic moving.,c:Speed up to pass slower drivers quickly.,d:Allow extra travel time so you are not rushed.
note: Allowing extra travel time, obeying speed limits, and using signals can reduce stress and incidents of aggressive driving.

question: What does an octagonal (eight-sided) traffic sign always indicate?
options: a:Speed limit sign.,b:Hospital sign.,c:Stop sign.,d:Yield sign.
note: An octagonal, eight-sided sign always means STOP — come to a complete stop at the sign and proceed when safe.

question: To help relieve fatigue on a long trip, which practice is recommended?
options: a:Drive continuously and only stop for fuel every five hours.,b:Keep driving but sip strong coffee.,c:Open a window and drive with music loud.,d:Stop for a rest every two hours or sooner if drowsy.
note: Take frequent breaks on long trips; if drowsy, stop in a safe place to rest or sleep rather than continuing to drive.

question: A flashing red traffic signal requires drivers to:
options: a:Stop and then proceed when the way is clear, just like a stop sign.,b:Slow down but not stop.,c:Yield only to vehicles from the right.,d:Proceed as if it's a green light.
note: Treat a flashing red signal as a stop sign: come to a complete stop and go when safe.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Leave the engine running to keep accessories on.,c:Leave the key in the ignition for a short errand.,d:Only lock the doors without removing the key.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The speed you must always drive regardless of conditions.,b:The maximum legal speed you can travel under dangerous conditions.,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,d:A suggested safe speed for wet conditions.
note: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions; you must drive more slowly when conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is always raining at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark,c:There are more pedestrians at night than day.,d:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night limits how far ahead you can see, which requires slower speeds and proper headlight use.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash through a symbol indicates:
options: a:An action is forbidden.,b:Drivers should come to a complete stop.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.,d:That the road is closed.
note: A red circle with a slash over a black symbol means the depicted action is prohibited.

question: Which factor greatly affects your ability to stop?
options: a:The time of day only.,b:Road conditions,c:The number of passengers in the car.,d:The color of your vehicle.
note: Stopping ability is strongly influenced by road surface condition—reduce speed on poor surfaces to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when a traffic signal turns green?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly.
note: A green light means you may go, but first yield to pedestrians and to traffic already in the intersection.

question: Of the following, which is hardest to see at night?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.,d:Streetlights.
note: Pedestrians are the hardest to see at night compared to signs and other roadside objects; extra caution is required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to pass on a two-way, two-lane road?
options: a:When you can clearly see the road ahead.,b:Only if all three of the above are true.,c:When your vehicle can reach the speed required to pass.,d:When you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
note: You may pass only when you can see clearly ahead, can re-enter your lane before encountering oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can complete the pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Only when traffic is heavy.,b:Only if the vehicle is small.,c:Just after you start passing.,d:Early enough that other drivers know your intent.
note: Signal well before you begin the maneuver so others have time to react.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Are better drivers because they are more careful.,b:Have faster reaction times than sober drivers.,c:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies,d:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination, vision, and reaction time; it is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol.

question: When driving on potentially slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Use cruise control to keep a constant speed.,b:Always drive at the maximum posted speed.,c:Reduce your following distance and avoid sudden speed changes.,d:Make abrupt steering corrections to stay in lane.
note: On slippery surfaces, reduce speed, avoid sudden maneuvers, and increase the space between you and other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Stop on the shoulder if tired.,b:Always use cruise control.,c:Signal,d:Change lanes frequently to stay alert.
note: Signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before lane changes; use cruise control with caution.

question: Pentagonal signs are used to indicate:
options: a:Speed limits.,b:Pedestrian-only areas.,c:No passing zones.,d:School zones and school crossings.
note: A five-sided (pentagonal) sign indicates a school zone or school crossing—exercise extra caution near schools.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow arrow indicate?
options: a:Slow and stop if safe to do so.,b:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic.,c:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is coming; drivers should stop unless they are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what lights should be used?
options: a:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,b:Use high beams to warn others.,c:Use your emergency flashers and keep your low-beam headlights on so others can see you.,d:Use only parking lights.
note: When stopped at night, turn on emergency flashers and keep low beams on so other road users can see the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?
options: a:If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear and gradually slow to encourage them to pass.,b:Immediately slow down abruptly to warn them.,c:Sound your horn and stay in your lane.,d:Move into the right lane if one is available.
note: If someone is following too closely, move to the right lane if possible; if not, wait until the road ahead is clear and slow down gradually so the tailgater can pass. Never brake suddenly.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what action should you take to warn them?
options: a:Shout from inside your vehicle.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers only.,c:Wave your arms out the window.,d:Sound your horn to alert the other driver or pedestrian.
note: Use your horn to warn others when you think they may not see you and a collision is imminent.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called:
options: a:Information signs.,b:Guide signs.,c:Regulatory signs.,d:Warning signs.
note: Regulatory signs convey laws and rules (e.g., speed limits, stop signs) that drivers must obey.

question: If another driver cuts you off, the best reaction is to:
options: a:Let it go and continue driving safely.,b:Flash your high beams and chase them.,c:Pull up beside them and shout.,d:Brake-check them to teach a lesson.
note: Avoid road rage—don’t take it personally; continue driving safely and let minor offenses go.

question: How can stress affect your driving performance?
options: a:It will make you fall asleep at the wheel.,b:It improves your reaction time.,c:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and impair driving judgment.,d:It decreases your chances of an accident.
note: Strong emotions and stress reduce concentration and decision-making ability; avoid driving when emotionally impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left, what is an important right-of-way consideration?
options: a:Cut across lanes to get into position quickly.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before completing the turn.,c:Sound your horn to warn others.,d:Swing to the right side of your lane to prepare.
note: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before making a left turn to avoid collisions.

question: On a divided multilane highway when you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Slow down,b:Speed up to clear the lane.,c:Stop immediately where you are.,d:Disregard the signal if other lanes exist.
note: If safe, move over and stop to give a clear path to approaching emergency vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from a multilane one-way street?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The left lane.,c:Either lane is acceptable.,d:The center lane.
note: On a one-way street or multilane road, begin left turns from the left-most lane unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check blind spots before changing lanes called?
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:A good driving habit and necessary for safe lane changes.,c:An illegal maneuver.,d:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.
note: Checking blind spots by briefly turning your head is a safe driving habit and should be done before lane changes or merging.

question: Which is a safe technique for driving through a curve?
options: a:Maintain the exact same speed throughout regardless of curve severity.,b:Slow down before entering the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.,c:Speed up before entering and slow down while exiting.,d:Brake hard in the middle of the curve to stay controlled.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and then gradually increase as you exit to maintain control and traction.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Proceed as soon as the bus door closes regardless of children.,b:Accelerate quickly to pass the bus.,c:Watch carefully for children walking along the side of the road before moving.,d:Honk to alert children to move aside.
note: After a school bus with its stop arm extended has stopped, watch for children who may be walking near the roadway before proceeding.

question: What should you never do while stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stop to drop off passengers.,b:Stop to look up an address.,c:Make a U-turn or back up if you missed an exit.,d:All of the above.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane; if you miss an exit, continue to the next safe turnaround instead of reversing or stopping.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Beer,b:Illegal drugs and certain prescription medications.,c:Inhalants like glue or paint.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription or over-the-counter medicines can impair driving and result in DUII.

question: Guide signs that show directions and mileage typically have what color background?
options: a:Red.,b:Blue.,c:Yellow.,d:Green.
note: Guide signs (destination signs) have a green background and provide directional and mileage information to drivers.

question: What is the typical effect of driving while distracted?
options: a:It is never dangerous.,b:It usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,c:It usually causes the driver to drive faster.
note: Distractions reduce a driver's ability to detect and respond to hazards, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must you yield to when entering a roundabout?
options: a:Pedestrians only.,b:Bicyclists inside the roundabout only.,c:Vehicles already in the roundabout.
note: When entering a roundabout you must yield to traffic already circulating as well as to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the approach.

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Excessive speed on wet surfaces.,b:Sudden turns.,c:Walking on the road.,d:Overuse of brakes.
note: Hydroplaning happens when tires cannot scatter water fast enough, usually at higher speeds, causing loss of traction.

question: What is the illegal minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) for drivers age 21 or older in West Virginia?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.10 percent.,d:0.02 percent.
note: Drivers aged 21 or older are legally impaired at a BAC of 0.08% or higher.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross oncoming traffic safely depends on:
options: a:Road and weather conditions and the amount of oncoming traffic.,b:Whether you used your turn signal.,c:The color of your vehicle.,d:The presence of a crosswalk only.
note: Crossing traffic safely depends on road surface, weather, and how much oncoming traffic there is and at what speed.

question: When parked facing downhill, how should your front wheels be turned?
options: a:Turned away from the curb.,b:Turned partially toward the center of the road.,c:Aiming straight ahead.,d:Turned toward the curb.
note: When parked downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will be stopped by the curb rather than rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red.,b:Stop in the center of the intersection.,c:Apply brakes sharply to stop immediately.,d:Prepare to stop safely unless already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns that red is coming; slow and stop safely if you can do so, unless you're already in the intersection.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and driving?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if only a few drinks are consumed.,d:Only an issue for inexperienced drivers.
note: Driving after drinking is a serious safety hazard and significantly raises the likelihood of crashes and injuries.

question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted for both directions.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:You must stop before proceeding.,d:One-way traffic ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite directions and prohibit passing from either side except in limited turning situations.

question: When must you pull over and allow an emergency vehicle to pass?
options: a:Only if it is following you.,b:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.,c:Regardless of the direction it's coming from.,d:Only if it has a siren but no lights.
note: You must pull over to the right edge and stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens regardless of their direction.

question: If a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) begins to lose traction, what should the driver do?
options: a:Switch off the ABS system immediately.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger,c:Pump the brakes rapidly to simulate ABS.,d:Release the brake and then reapply it repeatedly.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake; the system will modulate braking automatically while you steer to safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, what is the correct visual check order before proceeding?
options: a:Check the rearview mirror,b:Look right first,c:Look left,d:Move when the vehicle ahead moves.
note: When stopped, check left first because traffic from that direction will be closest; then check right, and left again before proceeding.

question: A steady green traffic light means:
options: a:You must stop and look for a green arrow.,b:You must slow and prepare to stop.,c:You may proceed through the intersection if the road is clear.,d:You may only turn right.
note: A steady green light allows you to go through the intersection when clear; turning movements still require yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:Just front-seat occupants during the day.,b:All occupants of the vehicle,c:Only passengers on long trips.,d:Only the driver.
note: Seat belts protect all occupants—ensure every person in the vehicle is properly restrained for the best safety outcome.

question: What is meant by the term 'No zone' around large trucks or buses?
options: a:A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.,b:A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.,c:A special speed zone.
note: The 'No zone' refers to the large blind spots around trucks and buses—on the sides, in front, and behind—where smaller vehicles may not be seen by the truck or bus driver.

question: Which of the following is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Seat belts are unnecessary for short trips.,b:Never place a rear-facing infant seat in a front seat with an active passenger airbag.,c:Children 12 and under should always sit in the front seat.,d:Airbags are always safe for infants and small children.
note: Children 12 and under should ride in the rear seat properly restrained; never place a rear-facing infant seat in front of an active airbag.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:You are making a turn.,b:You are slowing down or stopping.,c:You are changing lanes.,d:You have your emergency brake on.
note: Brake lights indicate to drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping; keep them maintained.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:Every five minutes while driving.,b:Only on highways when passing another vehicle.,c:Only when parking.,d:Whenever you are changing lanes
note: Check blind spots by turning your head to view areas not covered by mirrors whenever changing the vehicle's position.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what important actions should you take?
options: a:Signal early, check your blind spot, and ensure the lane is clear before entering.,b:Signal only as you start the lane change.,c:Make rapid lane changes to minimize time in adjacent lanes.,d:Turn your headlights on to warn other drivers.
note: Signal ahead of time, turn and check blind spots, and confirm the lane is clear before moving over.

question: When driving in fog, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and increase speed.,b:Follow the vehicle ahead closely.,c:Use high beam headlights for better illumination.,d:Drive cautiously
note: In fog, slow down, drive cautiously, and use low beams — high beams will reflect and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper action if you miss your interstate exit?
options: a:Quickly cross lanes to make the exit.,b:Make a U-turn to return to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and leave there.
note: If you miss an exit, do not stop or back up. Continue to the next exit and safely return to your destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:Only in school zones.,b:On hills,c:Only on multi-lane highways.,d:Only when signs say no passing.
note: Passing is unlawful and unsafe on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings, and in designated no-passing zones.

question: You should drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:Anything makes road conditions less than perfect (wet, slippery, poor visibility).,b:You see a police car only.,c:You are entering a highway with other cars.,d:Traffic is flowing faster than the limit.
note: Reduce your speed below the posted limit whenever conditions (weather, visibility, road surface) make driving less than ideal.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in your area, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to create distance.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,d:Maintain your speed and lane.
note: Pull over or otherwise clear the path for emergency vehicles so they can reach their destination quickly and safely.

question: If involved in a crash, what should a driver do at the scene?
options: a:Stop at or near the scene and move out of traffic if possible.,b:Stand or walk in traffic lanes to direct cars.,c:Leave without leaving information.,d:Drive away slowly and report later.
note: Stop and secure the scene; avoid standing in traffic lanes and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles when safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before and after passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Sound your horn three times.,c:Move back into the lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, check mirrors and blind spots and signal; re-enter your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:Blue.,d:White.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; yellow separates opposite directions.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Drive faster than the train.,b:Look for a way around lowered gates.,c:Ignore it if no train is visible.,d:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: Railroad warning signs alert you to the possible presence of trains; be prepared to stop and obey crossing devices.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross those lines?
options: a:To pass bicyclists at any time.,b:Whenever traffic ahead is moving slowly.,c:To pass slower traffic when safe.,d:Only to make a left turn into or from a private road
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; crossing is allowed only to make left turns into driveways, alleys, or private roads.

question: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Drive quickly across to minimize time on the tracks.,b:Turn up the radio to listen for an approaching train.,c:Assume trains will always stop for vehicles.,d:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
note: If there are no active warnings, look and listen carefully in both directions and cross only when clear.
